summary: The paper offers a genuinely novel and clearly motivated theoretical analysis of the PCC plateau in attention-based regression under joint MSE+PCC training, identifying two distinct bottlenecks (gradient attenuation and convex-hull capacity) and proposing three principled mechanisms (SRA, DATS, DNPL) that map onto the theory. The theory-to-method correspondence is a real strength, but the experimental validation does not yet meet the ICLR bar: key results on UCI and MOSI lack error bars, seeds, or significance tests despite claims of 'significant improvements,' the UCI gains are small in absolute terms, baselines are thin (no gradient-conflict methods, no non-convex aggregators, no simple rescaling alternatives), and the synthetic dataset is self-designed to confirm the theory it motivates. With added statistical rigor and stronger baselines this could become a solid accept.
strengths: First rigorous theoretical decomposition of the PCC plateau into an optimization-dynamics bottleneck (Corollary 2.1, O(1/sigma_y^{3/2}) attenuation) and a convex-hull capacity bound (Theorem 2.2); the two-limit framing is clean and non-obvious.

Each of the three proposed mechanisms (SRA, DATS, DNPL) is directly motivated by a specific theoretical result, giving the method a principled rather than ad-hoc character that is rare for attention-variant papers.
The DNPL StopGrad design is a thoughtful way to rescale gradient magnitude without shifting stationary points, and the explicit acknowledgment of this trade-off is commendable.

Diverse evaluation settings span synthetic, tabular (UCI), spatial transcriptomics, and multimodal sentiment, covering both the homogeneous-data regime the theory targets and more standard regression tasks.
Ablations in Table 1 isolate each component's contribution, and the spatial-transcriptomics curves in Figure 6 visibly demonstrate the plateau-breaking behavior on a real homogeneous dataset.

key_concerns.issue: UCI (Table 1) and MOSI (Table 2) results report single numbers with no error bars, no seeds, and no significance tests, yet the abstract and conclusion claim 'significant improvements.' The UCI PCC deltas are small (Appliance +0.042, Online News +0.012, Superconductivity +0.010) and could plausibly be within run-to-run noise for FT-Transformer variants.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean +/- std over at least 5 seeds for all UCI and MOSI numbers, and run paired significance tests (e.g., paired t-test or Wilcoxon) against the baseline; only claim 'significant' where it holds.

key_concerns.issue: Baselines are insufficient to attribute gains to the proposed mechanisms rather than to generic alternatives. There is no comparison to (i) gradient-conflict / multi-task balancing methods (PCGrad, GradNorm, uncertainty weighting) that could similarly address the MSE/PCC gradient ratio, (ii) non-convex aggregators (max-pooling, MLP aggregation, linear/ReLU attention) that already escape the convex hull, or (iii) a trivial baseline of just rescaling the PCC loss by 1/sigma_y (i.e., DNPL alone) on every dataset.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one gradient-conflict baseline and one non-convex aggregator baseline on the UCI and MOSI benchmarks, and run DNPL-only and SRA-only as standalone ablations across all datasets (not just per-dataset as currently done).

key_concerns.issue: The synthetic dataset is constructed by the authors specifically to exhibit the signal-vs-background structure the theory assumes, so Figure 5 is closer to a sanity check on a self-generated instance than independent validation; the claim that it 'confirms our theoretical study' is partly circular.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either relabel Figure 5 as a controlled illustration, or validate on an externally-defined synthetic benchmark with controllable homogeneity, and report variance over dataset generations.

key_concerns.issue: The theory is developed for a single-layer convex attention + linear head, and the extension to deep multi-layer architectures (the practically relevant case) is deferred to an appendix (Section E). Since all real experiments use deep backbones (FT-Transformer, EGN, ALMT), the gap between the proven regime and the evaluated regime is not adequately addressed in the main text.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move at least a summary of the deep-architecture applicability argument into the main paper, and discuss under what conditions the single-layer bounds are expected to remain informative for stacked attention.

key_concerns.issue: Theoretical assumptions are restrictive and partly unverified: Corollary 2.1 assumes rho in [0,1] (excluding the common early-training regime where rho is negative or near zero), and Theorem 2.2 requires R < sigma0/||w||, but no empirical check that these hold during training is reported.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report the empirical values of rho and R/(sigma0/||w||) during training on the real benchmarks to confirm the bounds are in their valid regime, or relax the assumptions.

key_concerns.issue: Key hyperparameters (lambda_PCC, lambda_gamma, beta, Tmin, gamma_max) are mentioned but not fully specified in the main text, and the per-dataset tuning protocol is unclear, raising concerns about overfitting hyperparameters to each benchmark.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a single table of all hyperparameters per dataset, state which were tuned and on what validation signal, and report sensitivity to lambda_PCC and beta.

questions_for_authors: What are the per-seed standard deviations for the UCI PCC improvements? Are the +0.012 (Online News) and +0.010 (Superconductivity) deltas statistically significant over 5+ seeds?
How does ECA compare to a simple baseline that just rescales the PCC loss by 1/sigma_y (DNPL-only) or to PCGrad-style gradient surgery on the UCI benchmarks?
Does the convex-hull capacity bound (Theorem 2.2) remain informative when the aggregator is a stack of attention layers rather than a single convex pooling step?
During training on the real benchmarks, what is the empirical range of rho and of R/(sigma0/||w||)? Do the assumptions of Corollary 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 actually hold?
How sensitive are the gains to lambda_PCC and to the DATS hyperparameters beta and Tmin? Is the same setting used across all four benchmarks or is per-dataset tuning required?
Is the StopGrad in DNPL truly neutral with respect to stationary points under Adam-style optimizers with weight decay, or only under plain SGD?
calibration_check: Claims of 'significant improvements' and 'consistently breaks the PCC plateau' are over-scoped relative to the evidence, since no significance testing is performed and several UCI gains are small in absolute terms; the 'first rigorous theoretical analysis' claim is plausible but unverified against the broader gradient-conflict and correlation-optimization literature.

significance.justification: The PCC-plateau analysis is a useful contribution for the attention-regression subfield, but impact is narrow: it targets the specific MSE+PCC joint-loss setting and is unlikely to change practice outside correlation-heavy regression tasks.

novelty.justification: First principled decomposition of the PCC plateau into optimization and capacity limits with a matching three-mechanism fix; individual components (adaptive temperature, residual extrapolation, loss rescaling) are known but the theory-driven combination is genuinely new.

rigor.justification: Main proofs appear correct but rely on restrictive assumptions (rho in [0,1], R < sigma0/||w||) that are never empirically verified on the real benchmarks, and the deep-architecture extension is deferred to an appendix.

statistical_soundness.justification: UCI and MOSI tables report point estimates with no seeds, error bars, or significance tests, yet claim 'significant improvements'; the spatial-transcriptomics results do report +/- std but only over 3 folds; this is below the ICLR bar for a method paper.

calibration_honesty.justification: Claims of significance and consistency are not supported by significance testing; the synthetic dataset is self-designed to validate the theory; limitations are mentioned but the abstract overstates the empirical strength of the evidence.

clarity.justification: Generally well-written with a clear theory-to-method narrative; some notation is dense and the main text leans heavily on deferred proofs, but the logical flow is easy to follow.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure (Introduction, Theory, Method, Related Work, Experiments, Conclusion) is followed and length appears reasonable; related work is unusually thin for the breadth of touched literature.

reproducibility.justification: Data sources, model backbones, and evaluation protocols are named, but key hyperparameters and the per-dataset tuning protocol are under-specified in the main text, and seeds are not reported.

related_work.justification: Brief and narrowly scoped; misses the multi-task gradient-conflict literature (PCGrad, GradNorm, uncertainty weighting) and prior non-convex aggregation work that are directly relevant to both limitations identified.

figure_quality.justification: Captions are informative and each figure supports a specific claim (plateau, gradient-ratio decay, sigma_y growth, synthetic curves, spatial-transcriptomics curves); figures appear well-designed from their descriptions.

breadth_generality.justification: Four settings are tested but UCI tabular regression is an unnatural fit for attention, the synthetic set is self-designed, baselines are thin, and only the homogeneous regime is stressed; generalization to non-homogeneous and non-attention aggregators is under-supported.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: the theoretical contribution is interesting and the method is well-motivated, but missing error bars/seeds/significance tests and weak baselines on the headline UCI and MOSI results prevent acceptance as submitted.
